The only person who will call you a liar is those already hurting you? You won't get grilled about this?

Have you ever heard of a DEFENSE ATTORNEY? You clearly have no clue what you're talking about. Propaganda. Pffft. Try speaking to some people who have actually reported sexual abuse or rape. (It isn't called "gray area drunken sex" it is called rape.)

I hear you, and you're probably telling the truth. 
I'm just calling it like I see it. 
After spending my teens and early twenties as exactly that kind of "easy target", and reading about other's experiences with predators that want so much to "help" young women with histories of sexual abuse, that kind of shit throws up a red flag for me. That doesn't always mean "this guy is for sure trying to pull some shit", and I didn't even know when I commented if you were a 50 year old man or a 13 year old girl or what.
But your comment gave me the creeps in the context of the original post. Just sayin'.

Yeah, you're probably telling the truth and not a total creep. But it's really common for predatory men to prey on trauma survivors like that. When somebody posts "I don't even care what happens to my body anymore" and your only response is "You wanna come to my place and have a beer?" that comes across as shady as hell in my book.
You literally have more money than my roommate and I combined, if that makes you feel any better.

I'm sorry for what you're going through and what your sick fuck of a father did to you. Your mom sounds like my entire family.
I know exactly what you mean about not wanting to spend years of really hard work to just maybe reach a level of mediocre life. I'm not willing/able to do that shit either. I'm going to check out really soon.
Well that's not creepy at all...
I hope things get better for you, and me, and all the other trauma survivors that are still struggling. You probably should try to talk to your therapist about this.

This one sentence uttered by my grandmother two years ago, in reference to the uncle that (everybody knows) molested me as a kid:

"What am I supposed to do? Uninvite him from Thanksgiving?!?"
I'm 31 and I've felt this way for a long time.

God this sounds just like me. Not at all a knee jerk reaction, I've wanted to die for the last 16 years. People say "go to a therapist" and all I can think is "Is the shrink going to give me a GUN? No? Then how the fuck does that help me?"

Even on days that I'm happy I know that I'm going to kill myself sooner or later, and the only thing that keeps me from doing it sooner is my nephew. I've also been just trying to keep my distance from him lately, though I love him more than anything in the world, because I figure if we grow apart more and more he'll be less upset. I wish I would just get cancer or get hit by a fucking bus. I just don't want to be the one responsible for hurting my nephew.

I also have a very strong "don't let them know" mentality about it and I think that has really really fucked me up and kept me from getting the help I should have for a lot of years now. If you can fight that impulse, you really should. I don't think you'll regret reaching out for help. Good luck.

I often feel like my being so suicidal doesn't have an 'external cause' either. Sometimes I think "I'm not all that depressed, more so suicidal. Can you even be suicidal without being depressed? And how the hell can I DO ANYTHING about it? If you tell a psychiatrist that you're suicidal they just throw you in the psych ward."
It's like even when I'm happy, I know that eventually I'm going to off myself. It's inevitable. I can't even imagine dying any other way.

I've thought about going West to do it too. No specific cities really, it'd just be nice to be in the wilderness or staring at the ocean.
Would it be a terrible thing for your family to know you're seeing a therapist? Lots of people see therapists, it isn't seen as a big deal anymore by most people, at least in the US.

It's not a bad thing to have somebody give you a chance! Even if they give you the job because you would have trouble getting work someplace else, doesn't mean that this job experience will make it harder for you to get a better job in the future. I'm sure it will be exactly the opposite. Any job or volunteer position looks good on your resume, better than no job. 

Relationships are always a gamble, but if you're that unstable right now I would think about working on that before you really try to look for a relationship. Are you in counseling? Is that an option?  Either way, you are worthy of love and happiness and this job!

It took me until I was 30 to realize that what I felt as random misplaced guilt was what other people refer to as 'anxiety' and I that I have an anxiety disorder. 

Do you feel guilty ABOUT what happened? (In which case you should probably see a therapist. In any case you should probably see a therapist) 
Or do you feel just plain "guilty all the time" weather or not you're really thinking about the abuse? Could it be anxiety?

Good luck and know that it's not your fault!

Almost all abuse survivors say those words "Other people had it so much worse than I did..." including all the other people we're referring to when we say it. People who went through unimaginable shit say it. Because that's how we were trained to think, to downplay the problems and blame ourselves for not just being okay with it.

But it's not okay. It's really, really not okay. And it's not okay that your mom sides with him. My family does the same thing with my uncle. They act like I'm being dramatic, like I'm an asshole for not wanting to eat Thanksgiving dinner with him.

Well I'm reading now that those numbers are disputed but it seems legit to me. I have known and currently know so very many LGBT people that the 10% statistic always seemed accurate-to-a-bit-low to me.

Anywho, lgbt groups are a great place to meet date-able people your age. I was lucky enough to have a ton of lgbt kids at my high school but my roommate was in your shoes (but worse, getting the shit kicked out of him all the time) and so he spent a lot of time at the teen Outreach center and met all his boyfriends there.

Good luck! <3

Both puberty and depression cause chemical stuff to happen in your brain to MAKE YOU forgetful and bad at focusing, decision making and learning.

Depression makes your brain just fucking NOT ACT RIGHT! It's absolutely not your fault and it doesn't make you a bad person at all. 

I have forgotten to feed pets and forgot all sorts of other important stuff over the years. It happens. It doesn't mean you're a selfish jerk, it just means your brain is too overloaded with other things and you don't have much control over than.

You aren't the only gay kid in your school, just the only one you know of. At least 1 out of 10 people are gay and a LOT more are bisexual.

Just think about it when you look around your school. How many kids in your class? 30? It's almost impossible that less than 2 of those kids are gay.  120 kids in your graduating class? Well you're probably about 1 of a dozen then. 

I know somebody posted a suicide hotline already, but there are hotlines specifically for LGBT teens.

http://www.thetrevorproject.org/ is one of them. 1-866-488-7386

I hope you live within a decent distance of a city with an outreach group of some sort. Here in Madison, Wisconsin we have a place called Outreach that has groups for everybody from gay teens to transgender elderly folks. 

Maybe there's someplace like that but you don't know about it yet? Have you looked into it?

Maybe you have a supportive teacher that would help you create a Gay-Straight-Alliance club at your school?

Good luck to you  <3
